design.frames: decoded once, shared by both arms
design.note: both arms are the same FootballTracker object differing only in tracker_backend

why_invalid: FootballTracker.detect_objects_in_frames calls detector.detect(frame, abs_idx) with a frame_id, which hits the detector's in-memory cache. The first arm measured populated that cache and every later run -- including the whole second arm -- was served from it. The 0.00 ms/frame detector figure is the symptom: a 155 ms/frame CPU detector cannot cost nothing. The comparison was between one cold arm and one warm one, so the +5.34% it reported means nothing and must not be quoted.
superseded_by: runtime.json, produced with detector.clear_cache() before every measured run
